1. **Corporate & Commercial Advisory** — corporate governance, legal compliance and risk management, contract management, business valuation, accounting/auditing support, business structuring and restructuring, ESOP solutions, international trade advisory.
2. **Transactions & Strategic Advisory** — domestic and cross-border transaction structuring, contract drafting/review, financing and investment support, real estate and employment-linked transaction advisory.
3. **Contracts & Agreements** — employment/sales contracts, lease agreements, partnership deeds, AOA/MOA and other corporate documents, shareholder agreements, NDAs, settlement/arbitration agreements, powers of attorney.
4. **Joint Ventures** — structuring and negotiation of joint ventures and strategic alliances, JV agreements, governance arrangements, dispute-avoidance drafting.
5. **Mergers & Acquisitions** — pre-transaction due diligence and valuation, purchase/merger/shareholder agreement negotiation, NDAs and LOIs, regulatory compliance and financing, post-transaction integration.
6. **Cross-Border Transactions** — international contract drafting/review, trade compliance, cross-border M&A and foreign investment structuring, regulatory approvals, tax planning, currency/exchange-control considerations.
7. **Funding & Investments** — loan agreements and debt fundraising, equity and securities offerings, pre- and post-IPO advisory, ESOPs, fintech and digital-securities advisory.
8. **Employment, HR & POSH** — employment contracts, offer/appointment letters, handbooks/policies, disciplinary proceedings and terminations, union and workplace-safety matters, POSH services (policy, external ICC membership, awareness training, inquiry reports, regulatory filings).
9. **Compliance & Regulatory Support** — corporate secretarial compliance, board resolutions/governance, regulatory filings/licensing, HR and data-privacy compliance, contract lifecycle management, SEBI/stock-exchange compliance advisory.
10. **Dispute Resolution & Arbitration** — civil/criminal litigation, arbitration, mediation, recovery proceedings including Section 138 matters, settlement negotiations, police-complaint/FIR assistance.
11. **Due Diligence** — document, litigation and regulatory-compliance review, IP and employment/labour review, environmental due diligence, risk-assessment reporting.
12. **Intellectual Property Rights** — trademark/patent/copyright searches, filing and prosecution, enforcement and infringement litigation, trade-secret protection, IP portfolio management, licensing strategy, anti-counterfeiting.
13. **Legal Opinions** — considered, written legal opinions supporting high-stakes business decisions and board resolutions, drawing on the other twelve practice areas.

## Insights — article summaries

### Trademark Renewal in India: Timelines, TM-R Filing and What Businesses Routinely Get Wrong
https://www.vidhicorplegal.com/insights/trademark-renewal-timelines.html
A registered trademark in India is valid ten years from application (Trade Marks Act, 1999) and can be renewed indefinitely. Renewal (Form TM-R) can be filed up to one year before expiry; a missed deadline allows a one-year restoration window with a surcharge under Rule 58, after which the mark becomes liable for removal and its priority date is lost. Common failure points: treating renewal as solely the agent's responsibility, tracking "the trademark" rather than each Nice-Classification class (each can have its own renewal date), stale ownership/address records, and losing track of Madrid Protocol international designations separately from direct Indian filings. Recommendation: a single, business-owned register of every mark, class, jurisdiction and renewal date, reviewed on a fixed schedule.

### Indemnity Clause in a Commercial Contract: How to Read It the Way Your Counterparty Will
https://www.vidhicorplegal.com/insights/reading-the-indemnity-clause.html
Under Section 124, Indian Contract Act 1872, an indemnity is a promise to make good another's loss. In commercial contracts, the real negotiation is in the details: the scope of "Losses" (direct only, vs. indirect/consequential), caps and baskets (thresholds/deductibles), the survival period after closing, notice-and-defense procedure for third-party claims, and whether the indemnity is the sole remedy or cumulative with other claims. In Indian M&A specifically, indemnities are typically tiered — fundamental warranties (title, authority) carrying higher or uncapped protection and longer survival, business warranties carrying standard caps and shorter survival periods. The practical discipline: read every indemnity clause as if the loss has already happened, and check whether the cap/basket/survival terms match the risk allocation negotiated elsewhere in the deal.

### Corporate Compliance Calendar for India: Building One That Survives a Growing Company
https://www.vidhicorplegal.com/insights/compliance-calendar-for-growing-entities.html
Compliance splits into deadline-based obligations (ROC annual filings AOC-4/MGT-7, GST returns, TDS, PF/ESI, the POSH Act's annual report) and event-based obligations triggered by business actions (new office/state registration, director changes, headcount-threshold policy updates). Single-owner spreadsheets break down as headcount/entities/locations multiply, especially since shops & establishments rules are state legislation and vary. Compliance gaps are usually invisible until tested — by a labour inspection or, commonly, by investor due diligence ahead of a funding round. Framework: separate the two categories explicitly, assign named ownership per line, review quarterly with legal counsel specifically for trigger-based gaps, and maintain a state-wise/entity-wise register once operating in more than one state.

### Arbitration vs Litigation in India: When Arbitration Is Actually Faster, and When It Isn't
https://www.vidhicorplegal.com/insights/arbitration-vs-litigation-timing.html
The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended) requires an award within 12 months of completion of pleadings (Section 29A), extendable 6 months by consent. Arbitration wins for technical/specialist disputes, confidentiality-sensitive matters, cross-border enforceability (New York Convention), and when both parties engage constructively. The advantage narrows for multi-party disputes with non-signatories, urgent interim relief (often still sought via court under Section 9), post-award Section 34/37 challenges that can add years, and smaller claims where ad hoc arbitrator fees rival litigation costs. The decision is effectively made when the dispute-resolution clause is drafted, not when a dispute arises.

### POSH Compliance Checklist for India: What's Required Beyond the Policy Document
https://www.vidhicorplegal.com/insights/posh-compliance-beyond-the-policy.html
The POSH Act, 2013 requires any employer with 10+ employees to constitute an Internal Committee (IC): a senior woman Presiding Officer, at least two employee members, and one external member from an NGO/association familiar with sexual-harassment issues — a validly constituted IC is not optional. Operational requirements beyond the policy: 90-day inquiry completion, 10-day report submission, 60-day employer action window, an annual report to the District Officer (plus separate board-report disclosure for certain companies under the Companies Act/SEBI regulations), 3-year IC member terms requiring reconstitution, ongoing (not one-time) awareness training including training for IC members specifically on inquiry procedure, and confidentiality obligations under Section 16 of the Act.

### ESOP Pool Sizing for Indian Startups: What to Decide Before You Need It
https://www.vidhicorplegal.com/insights/esop-pool-sizing-for-startups.html
ESOPs for private Indian companies are governed by the Companies Act, 2013 and the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014 (board/shareholder approval, minimum 1-year cliff, restrictions on promoter/director grants subject to a DPIIT-recognised-startup carve-out). Sizing questions: pool needs over the next 18–24 months (not just current headcount, commonly 8–15% of fully diluted cap table at early stage); who absorbs dilution on a pool top-up (investors often negotiate this pre-money, concentrating dilution on existing shareholders — formula: Founders' % = 100% − Target Pool % − Investor %); avoiding pool shrinkage in down rounds; an "evergreen" mechanism returning forfeited/unvested options to the pool; standard 4-year vesting with a 1-year cliff.
